Walk at an easy pace. For a warm-up, increase gradually; for a cool-down, slow down gradually.

dose.basis: Strength recovery review + editorial work window
dose.cue: Large edge or jugs. Start with feet on a chair taking weight, then build to about 70% effort. Never start a session with max hangs.
About 20 mm edge, half crimp, arms straight but shoulders engaged. Add weight (or use a smaller edge) so you could hold ~3 s longer. Rest the full 3 min.
Open-hand or three-finger drag on a 20 mm edge. Load so ~3 s stays in reserve. Grip strength is grip-specific, so train the positions you climb in.
Bodyweight on the smallest edge you can hold for about 13 s, so 10 s leaves a small reserve. Half crimp. Move to a smaller edge only when it gets easy.
7 s hang, 3 s rest, 6 times = one set. Pick an edge or load where the last reps are hard but you still finish every hang with good form.
Hard, about 80% effort (roughly a load you could hold 20–25 s). 10 s on, 6 s off. End the set early if you cannot finish a hang with good form.
Moderate, about 60% effort: remove weight with a chair or pulley so you can repeat 24 hangs. You should feel a steady pump, not failure.
Feet on the floor or a chair so the hang feels easy, well below your max. 10 s on, 20 s off. Gentle enough for most days; skip it if your fingers are sore.
From a dead hang with straight arms, pull the shoulder blades down and back to lift the body a few centimetres, then lower slowly.

dose.basis: Strength recovery review + editorial work window
dose.cue: Full range, chin over the bar and fully straight arms at the bottom. Stop 1–2 reps before failure. Use a band or feet on a chair to assist if needed.

dose.basis: Strength recovery review + editorial work window
dose.cue: Add weight (backpack or belt) so 3–5 reps are hard but clean. Rest the full 3 minutes. Without weight, use slower tempo or the hangboard's biggest edge.
Pull as fast as possible, aiming the chest toward the bar; lower under control. Stop the set when speed drops. Trains dynamic moves and dynos.

dose.basis: Strength recovery review + editorial work window
dose.cue: Jump or step to the top, then lower for about 5 s to straight arms. Good for building to more pull-ups or adding eccentric strength.

dose.basis: Strength recovery review + editorial work window
dose.cue: Pull up, then hold about 5 s at the top, 5 s at 90° and 5 s at 120° elbow angle, lowering between positions. Assist with feet if you cannot hold the position.

dose.basis: Strength recovery review + editorial work window
dose.cue: Hang with active shoulders and lift the knees toward the chest without swinging. Progress to straight legs or toes-to-bar.

dose.basis: Strength recovery review + editorial work window
dose.cue: Hands under shoulders, body in one line. Balances the pulling in climbing. Use knees or a wall to make it easier.
Front shin angled, back leg long. Prop the hip with a block if it floats. Props shown are optional.
Soles together, knees wide. Fold forward only as far as feels easy. Props shown are optional.
Low lunge with hands on a chair; sink the hips forward and down. Props shown are optional.
Deep squat, arms resting forward on a chair or block. Let the hips hang. Props shown are optional.
On your back, hold the feet and draw the knees toward the armpits. Props shown are optional.
Ankle over opposite knee; pull the lower thigh toward the chest. Props shown are optional.
Half frog: one knee out to the side at 90°, other leg long. Rest forward on a chair. Props shown are optional.
Kneeling lunge, back knee padded; reach back for the rear foot if available. Props shown are optional.
Staggered stance, hands on a chair or wall; hinge over the straight front leg. Props shown are optional.
Kneel sitting back on the heels; lean back only as far as the knees allow. Props shown are optional.
Seated, one shin forward and one leg bent back. Sit tall on a cushion. Props shown are optional.
Soles together, then recline. Use a strap or pillows under the knees. Props shown are optional.
Seated figure-four: ankle over the opposite knee, walk the hands back. Props shown are optional.
One leg bent in front, the other out behind; lower toward the floor. Props shown are optional.
Wide stance, shift into one bent knee with the other leg straight. Use a chair. Props shown are optional.
Side-lying on a forearm, legs stacked; lift the hip gently to lengthen the side. Props shown are optional.
Back knee on a padded chair, front foot forward; press the hips forward. Props shown are optional.
On your back with one leg up on a chair or wall; keep the other leg long. Props shown are optional.
Low lunge, rotate the chest toward the front knee. Props shown are optional.
Deep squat, elbow inside one knee, rotate open. Props shown are optional.
Stack the shins. Sit on a block or chair; fold forward gently. Props shown are optional.
Butterfly with a forward fold; rest the arms on a chair or block. Props shown are optional.
Cross one thigh over the other, then fold forward over the legs. Props shown are optional.
On your back, cross the thighs and hug the legs toward the chest. Props shown are optional.
Kneeling lunge; loop a strap around the back foot and draw it up. Props shown are optional.
From kneeling on the heels, lean back onto the hands or forearms. Props shown are optional.
Deep squat with knees wide; hold a chair or pole for balance. Props shown are optional.
One leg folded back, the other long. Lean back only as far as comfortable. Props shown are optional.
Long low lunge, back knee down; support the chest on a chair. Props shown are optional.
On your back, hold one straight leg up; keep the other leg long. Props shown are optional.
Back shin on a table or bench, front leg standing; tuck the pelvis. Props shown are optional.
Front shin across a table, hinge forward from the hips. Props shown are optional.
Seated, one leg long and one bent; reach forward along the long leg. Props shown are optional.
Soles together with feet further away; fold forward and relax the back. Props shown are optional.
Seated, cross one leg over the other and hug the shin toward you. Props shown are optional.
Standing figure-four holding a chair: ankle on the opposite knee, sit back. Props shown are optional.
From pigeon, rotate the chest toward the back leg. Props shown are optional.
On your back, hold both feet with the knees wide and drawn down. Props shown are optional.
On a chair, ankle over the opposite knee; hinge forward with a long spine. Props shown are optional.
Deep squat holding a pole or doorframe; keep the heels down if you can. Props shown are optional.
Kneel sitting on the heels; add a cushion under the seat if needed. Props shown are optional.
Deep squat, palms together, elbows gently pressing the knees wide. Props shown are optional.
